# fhir

> A Rust implementation of the HL7® FHIR® data model, plus a spec-driven code
> generator that produces it from the official FHIR specification JSON.

HL7®, and FHIR® are the registered trademarks of Health Level Seven
International and their use of these trademarks does not constitute an
endorsement by HL7. Canonical repository:
https://github.com/fhir-rust/fhir-rust/tree/main/fhir — all links below are
paths relative to this crate's own directory (`fhir/`) inside that monorepo.

Six releases are modelled — **R2** (1.0.2, DSTU2), **R3** (3.0.2, STU3),
**R4** (4.0.1), **R4B** (4.3.0), **R5** (5.0.0, the default), and **R6**
(6.0.0-ballot3, outside the semver promise while it stays a ballot draft) —
each a complete, independent Rust model behind its own cargo feature.
Releases are never shared as one type: `fhir::convert::between::<S, T>`
converts a document between them explicitly, through JSON, reporting what
was lost.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): overview, installation, feature flags, quick start
- [spec/index.md](spec/index.md): the normative specification, requirement ids `R1.x`–`R14.x`
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): agent guidance specific to this crate — read before generating code
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): build/test commands and the code-generator workflow
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release history, one entry per published version

## Look something up

- [fhir.md](fhir.md): generated, searchable index of every resource and field across every release — fastest way to answer "does X have field Y" (large; not curated — use this llms.txt for orientation, fhir.md for lookup)
- [spec/12-fhir-releases.md](spec/12-fhir-releases.md): how the six releases relate, and what `fhir::convert` does and does not preserve
- [spec/11-choice-types.md](spec/11-choice-types.md): `value[x]` choice fields, `Coded<E>`, and the enum fallback
- [spec/06-serialization.md](spec/06-serialization.md): round-tripping to and from canonical FHIR JSON

## Examples

- [examples/build_patient.rs](examples/build_patient.rs): construct a resource and serialize it
- [examples/extensions.rs](examples/extensions.rs): reading and writing extensions
- [examples/code_systems.rs](examples/code_systems.rs): type-safe `CodeSystem` enums
- [examples/convert_release.rs](examples/convert_release.rs): converting a document between releases with a `LossReport`
- [examples/client_crud.rs](examples/client_crud.rs): the async FHIR REST client (feature `client`)
- [examples/r4_and_r5_side_by_side.rs](examples/r4_and_r5_side_by_side.rs): the same resource under two releases at once

## Releases (cargo features)

- `r2` — Release 2 (1.0.2, DSTU2)
- `r3` — Release 3 (3.0.2, STU3)
- `r4` — Release 4 (4.0.1)
- `r4b` — Release 4B (4.3.0): R4 plus the medication-definition rework
- `r5` — Release 5 (5.0.0) — **on by default**
- `r6` — Release 6 ballot draft (6.0.0-ballot3) — not final, no semver promise

## Modules

Per-release (under `r2`…`r6`, shape identical across releases): `resources`
(the release's FHIR resources as structs, plus the polymorphic `Resource`
enum), `codes` (CodeSystems as type-safe enums), `validate` (the `Validate`
trait, `#[derive(Validate)]`, pathed `ValidationIssue`s), `meta` (per-element
cardinality/bindings/`value[x]`/reference-target metadata), `coded` (the
`Coded<E>` wrapper for required-binding fields), `builder` (`BuilderError`
for generated `Type::builder()`s), `bundle_util` (Bundle iteration, paging,
the transaction/batch builder), `extension_ext` (`ExtensionExt`/
`ModifierExtensionExt`: `extension(url)`, `set_extension`, …), `summary`
(the `_summary=true` view), `temporal` (date/time parsing and
precision-aware comparison), `xml` (feature `xml`: `to_xml`/`from_xml`),
`parse`/`codegen`/`abstract_types`/`properties`/`todo` (the spec-JSON to
Rust generator and its internals).

Release-independent, at the crate root: `prelude` (re-exports the
most-used resources, datatypes, `Validate`, `Coded`, `ExtensionExt`),
`convert` (cross-release conversion with a `LossReport`), `client`
(feature `client`: the async REST client), `choice`/`types`/`codegen`.

## Machine-readable

- [llms.json](llms.json): the same map as structured JSON — module list, key types, cardinality mapping, per-release counts
